extra.message: NEXTAUTH_SECRET is listed under the Next.js `env` config key. Next.js inlines every key under `env` into the client-side JavaScript bundle at build time, so the JWT signing secret used by next-auth to sign/verify session tokens is shipped to every browser. Anyone who inspects the client bundle can recover NEXTAUTH_SECRET and forge arbitrary valid session JWTs (e.g. as an admin), completely bypassing authentication.

The CredentialsProvider's authorize() function compares submitted credentials against a hardcoded username ('user') and password ('password') string literal instead of validating against a user store with hashed passwords. Anyone who knows or guesses these hardcoded credentials can authenticate as a valid user, bypassing real authentication entirely.

The dashboard page hardcodes and renders sensitive secrets directly into the page markup: an API key ('X92nJdsL8aQp03Mf') and a MongoDB connection string containing a plaintext username/password ('mongodb://user:password@localhost:27017/db'). These values are shipped in the server-rendered HTML/client bundle to every authenticated user (there is no role check — any logged-in account, including the hardcoded 'user'/'password' credentials, sees them), exposing backend credentials and infrastructure details.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
